Carlos — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front (we'll attach the completed SIG sheet):

- Retention windows: ephemeral request logs (used for routing/latency analysis) are retained for 7 days by default. Aggregated telemetry (metrics and perf histograms) is retained for 13 months.
- Stored prompt/log artifacts: we do not persist prompt text beyond the 7-day short-term logs unless a customer enables extended logging via an account setting or signs an explicit DPA amendment.
- Training on customer data: Redwood does not use customer prompts, documents, or generated outputs to train or further fine-tune models by default. Training/utility of customer-provided data requires an explicit opt-in workflow (written consent + DPA clause). When enabled, data used for training is stored in a segregated training bucket and not shared across customers.

I'll attach: (1) a filled SIG responses workbook, (2) a redacted prompt/log sample (PII removed), and (3) our current SOC 2 Type II summary PDF. Vivek and Laura are looped for any technical additions.

Next steps: let us know if you need a sanitized sample that follows Mediq's exact redaction rules or a short recording to walk through the opt-in DPA amendment.

Best,
Rachel

Carlos — quick technical confirmation and suggested SIG wording below.

1) Deletion mechanics: Redwood implements deletion via logical TTLs backed by an immutable audit log. Short-term logs use automated TTL-driven deletion (7-day lifecycle); the data is removed from active object stores and tombstoned. For customers requesting immediate purge we perform a coordinated logical destroy which removes all indexed references and marks objects for garbage collection; final object zeroing follows provider-specific lifecycle (we provide deletion certificates on request). For Dedicated or Private deployments where the customer controls storage, deletion is performed by the customer's storage controls per contract.

2) Provenance/reporting for opt-in training: When a customer opts in to training, we maintain a provenance manifest that records dataset IDs, ingestion timestamps, and the training job id(s) that used the data. We can provide a customer-specific provenance report (CSV) on request and include it as part of our training governance deliverables.

Suggested SIG cell text (paste-ready):
"By default, customer prompts and outputs are not used to train models. Customers may opt in via a contractual DPA amendment; for opt-ins we store contributed data in segregated training buckets and provide a provenance report listing dataset identifiers and training job IDs upon request."

If you want the team to redact the sample further to match Mediq's schema, tell us what fields to mask and we'll regenerate.

— Vivek
